question: How should a production app handle approvals, durable session resume, and cost tracking with this SDK?

report.title: Handling Approvals, Session Resumption, and Cost Tracking in Production Apps Using the SDK

sections.heading: Approvals Management
sections.body: Production applications utilizing the SDK must implement user authentication and authorization thoroughly by defining clear rules around who can approve tool calls. The SDK provides mechanisms for defining tool permissions globally and per-tool, which in conjunction with attributes like `needsApproval`, ensures controlled access to sensitive operations. Approvals can be managed through flag-based systems where actions requiring approval will pause the workflow until a decision is made by the user, enabling asynchronous management of tool requests, suitable for scenarios involving delayed decision-making. The SDK also supports notifications for real-time updates about approval requests, which enhances user engagement throughout the approval process. To streamline the workflow, a dedicated UI component can manage pending approvals using the `approvals` API.

sections.heading: Durable Session Resume
sections.body: To achieve durable session resumes in applications using the SDK, developers should use the `createAgent()` function in combination with a durable storage solution such as `SqliteStore`. By passing a `sessionId` to the `send()` method, applications can maintain user interactions across system disruptions, allowing sessions to be restored seamlessly. Implementing checkpoints that automatically save the transcript and state of interactions after crucial events—like responses or tool executions—ensures users can resume exactly where they left off, even in the case of interruptions. Utilizing `run.enqueue(input)` aids in preserving queued user inputs for execution order recovery and continuity, enhancing user experience.

sections.heading: Cost Tracking Methods
sections.body: Cost tracking in SDK-based applications can be effectively implemented by defining agent directories with parameters like `maxCostUsd`, which helps monitor expenditure per operation. The `Agent Client Protocol (ACP)` allows tracking of tool calls and associated costs in real-time, facilitating insights into resource use and expense management. Additionally, utilizing resources like the `Agent Forge` dashboard provides visualizations of agent operations and cost indicators, helping developers to optimize financial oversight in their applications.
